questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution provides for a bicameral Parliament of India?
questions.solution: Article 79 states that there shall be a Parliament for the Union which shall consist of the President and two Houses (Council of States and House of the People).

questions.question: As per Article 172 (2)_______of a State shall NOT be subject to dissolution.
questions.solution: Article 172(2) states that the Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) of a State shall not be subject to dissolution; it is a permanent body where one-third of members retire every second year.

questions.question: Article 323 of the Indian Constitution deals with __________ .
questions.option_4: power to extend functions of Public Services Commissions
questions.solution: Article 323 mandates the Union Public Service Commission and State Public Service Commissions to present annual reports on the work done by them to the President or Governor respectively.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution empowers the Supreme Court to review its own judgements or orders ?
questions.solution: Article 137 provides the Supreme Court the power to review any judgment pronounced or order made by it.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding provisions of the Indian Constitution:
1. Article 247 empowers the Parliament to establish additional courts for better administration of laws made by it.
2. Article 248 deals with residuary powers of legislation.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution: Both statements are correct. Article 247 allows for additional courts for central laws, and Article 248 gives the Union Parliament exclusive power to make laws on subjects not mentioned in any of the three lists (Residuary powers).

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution deals with the removal and suspension of a member of the Public Service Commission?
questions.solution: Article 317 specifies the procedure for the removal and suspension of a member of a Public Service Commission (UPSC or SPSC).

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Indian Constitution:
I. Part IV (Articles 36 to 51) deals with the organisation, composition and powers of the State Legislature.
II. Article 171 specifies the composition of the Legislative Councils in States.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution: Statement II only is correct. Part IV deals with DPSPs. The State Legislature is dealt with in Part VI (Articles 168-212).

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India provides that there shall be a Legislative Assembly for the National Capital Territory of Delhi?
questions.solution: Article 239AA, inserted by the 69th Amendment Act of 1991, provides for a Legislative Assembly and a Council of Ministers for the NCT of Delhi.

questions.question: Which among the following is a subject of Union Lists in the Constitution of India ?
questions.solution: Extradition is a subject under the Union List (Entry 18). Liquor is a State subject, while Social Planning and Boilers are under the Concurrent List.

questions.question: Provisions related to the seat of the "Supreme Court of India" is mentioned in which Article?
questions.solution: Article 130 states that the Supreme Court shall sit in Delhi or in such other place or places as the Chief Justice of India may, with the approval of the President, appoint.

questions.question: Part XVI of the Indian constitution deals with ___________ .
questions.option_2: Special provisions related to certain classes
questions.option_4: Special provisions related to municipal corporation
questions.solution: Part XVI (Articles 330 to 342) contains 'Special Provisions Relating to Certain Classes', such as reservations for SCs, STs, and previously Anglo-Indians.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian constitution provides for the National commission for Scheduled Castes?
questions.solution: Article 338 provides for the National Commission for Scheduled Castes. 338A provides for STs and 338B for OBCs.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian constitution mentions that it is duty of the Union government to protect States against external aggression and internal disturbance?
questions.solution: Article 355 imposes a duty on the Union to protect every State against external aggression and internal disturbance and to ensure that the government of every State is carried on in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution.

questions.question: Central Bureau of Intelligence and Investigation comes under which list of the seventh schedule of the Indian constitution?
questions.solution: The Central Bureau of Intelligence and Investigation is under the Union List (Entry 8) of the Seventh Schedule.

questions.question: The Indian parliament has power to impose restrictions on trade, commerce and intercourse through which Article of the Indian constitution?
questions.solution: Article 302 empowers Parliament to impose such restrictions on the freedom of trade, commerce, or intercourse between one State and another or within any part of the territory of India as may be required in the public interest.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding powers of the Governor:
I. Article 213 states that the Governor has the power to promulgate ordinances during the recess of the State Legislature.
II. Article 214 states that the Governor has the power to promulgate ordinances during the recess of the State Legislature.
Which of the above statements is/are correct ?
questions.solution: Statement I only is correct. Article 213 gives the ordinance-making power to the Governor. Article 214 relates to the establishment of High Courts for States.

questions.question: Article 350A of the Indian constitution is related with______.
questions.option_2: Facilities for instruction in mother-tongue at primary stage
questions.option_3: Direction for development of the Hindi language
questions.option_4: Language to be used in Supreme Court and High Courts of India
questions.solution: Article 350A provides that it shall be the endeavour of every state to provide adequate facilities for instruction in the mother-tongue at the primary stage of education to children belonging to linguistic minority groups.

questions.question: Which Article of Indian constitution is related with the Special provisions with respect to the State of Sikkim?
questions.solution: Article 371F contains special provisions for the state of Sikkim, which became a full-fledged state of India in 1975.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding appointment of judges in India:
I. Article 127 deals with the appointment of ad-hoc judges to the Supreme Court.
II. Article 126 deals with the appointment of ad-hoc judges to the Supreme Court.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution: Statement I is correct. Article 127 allows the Chief Justice of India, with the previous consent of the President, to appoint a High Court judge as an ad-hoc judge of the Supreme Court if there is a lack of quorum. Article 126 deals with the appointment of an Acting Chief Justice.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India deals with the Sessions of the Parliament?
questions.solution: Article 85 empowers the President to summon each House of Parliament to meet at such time and place as he thinks fit, and also to prorogue the Houses and dissolve the Lok Sabha.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Articles of Parliament in the Indian Constitution:
I. Chapter II of Part V (Articles 79–122) deals with the Articles of Parliament.
II. Chapter I of Part V deals with the Articles of Parliament.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution: Statement I is correct. Part V of the Constitution (The Union) is divided into chapters. Chapter II specifically contains provisions regarding the Parliament (Articles 79–122). Chapter I deals with the Union Executive.

questions.question: The Article of the Indian Constitution that deals with all the executive powers of the Governor is ____
questions.solution: Article 154 states that the executive power of the State shall be vested in the Governor and shall be exercised by him either directly or through officers subordinate to him in accordance with the Constitution.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC):
I. Part XIV of the Indian Constitution provides for the Union Public Service Commission.
II. Part X of the Indian Constitution provides for the Union Public Service Commission.
Which of the above statements is/are correct ?
questions.solution: Statement I is correct. Articles 315 to 323 in Part XIV of the Constitution deal with the appointment, removal, and powers of the UPSC and State Public Service Commissions.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the GST Council in India:
I. Article 279A provides for the creation of the Goods and Services Tax (GST) Council.
II. Article 246A provides for the creation of the Goods and Services Tax (GST) Council.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution: Statement I is correct. Article 279A was added by the 101st Amendment Act to establish the GST Council. Article 246A grants Parliament and State Legislatures the power to make laws with respect to GST.

questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act made the Right to Education a Fundamental Right in India?
questions.solution: The 86th Amendment Act, 2002 inserted Article 21A, making free and compulsory education for children aged 6–14 a Fundamental Right.
